name: git-repo-url-allows-granted
description:
The ALLOW half. Same fixture, same subcommand, same phase as git-repo-url-required — the ONLY difference is that the remote is the granted URL instead of `origin`. Forcing a URL would be worthless if it only ever produced denials; this is what shows the mechanism has a way through.

The assertion is the authz decision, not the tool result. An allowed sandbox call still comes back an error here (bronze runs no ToolCall controller, so nothing executes), and a scripted transcript replies the same either way — only the decision log distinguishes "authorized, then failed to run" from "never authorized".

The decision key is the object id [normalize_url, spicedb_object_id] produces for the URL, which is also the id the fixture's grant is written on. Those two agreeing is the whole contract: a grant written by a human has to match an id derived from argv.
